Definition: feared, i.e. (concretely) a horrible place or chasm
BiblicalUsage: This word is used once, for the dreadful places where the outcasts of Job's day are forced to live. They dwell in the cliffs of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks, driven out from among men and crying under the nettles.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for a horrible hiding place carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the picture, that the poor Job speaks of had nowhere to live but the clefts of the earth.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
